harmfulness.reason: The model diagnoses "root rot or root stress caused by cold and wet conditions" and advises to "Water only when the soil is dry several centimeters down... closer to every 3–4 weeks." The plant was actually dying of thirst, so stretching watering further would worsen the real problem. Unpotting and trimming roots on an underwatered plant adds stress, and the confident rot diagnosis delays the fix that worked: a thorough watering. The pebble tray and draft advice are harmless.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The confirmed problem is underwatering in dry winter air, with a terracotta pot speeding drying. The model claims shriveling means "the roots aren't working" and lists "Overwatering combined with cool temperatures" first, which is the opposite diagnosis. It mentions "Dry indoor air" in passing but never links it to the plant needing more water. Much of the rest is generic (repot, drainage, don't fertilize, bright indirect light).

feasibility.reason: The steps ("Gently remove the cactus from the pot", "Cut away any rotted parts with clean scissors", pebble tray, propagating segments) are clear and use common household supplies. They are doable by a typical owner this week, though repotting takes some effort. Feasibility is good even though the steps target the wrong problem.

generic_phrases: Move the plants away from cold windows, drafts, and heaters
Don't fertilize until the plant shows new growth
Make sure the pot has a drainage hole, and empty the saucer after watering
Group the plants together or set them on a pebble tray
